SE to run targeted INT8/FP8 bench with EiraTek prompt set and return summary by 2027-01-05
Schedule 60-min canary run planning session with EiraTek infra on 2026-12-22
action_items: Alex Chen | Send sandbox invite + bulletproof onboarding notes | 2026-12-19
Priya Nair | Kickoff profile run vs EiraTek prompts (INT8/FP8) and collect 1k prompt samples | 2027-01-04

summary: Introductory optimization onboarding: walked through Redwood Optimize console for creating comparison profiles (INT8 vs FP8), discussed fidelity lanes, canary rollout plan, and security/rollback constraints. Customer prioritized 95th p99 latency SLOs around 120ms for short chat flows and wants cost delta estimates for INT8 -> FP8 rollouts. Agreed to run targeted bench with their prompt set and meet for canary planning.
questions: What level of quality drop is tolerable for user-facing chat?
How does Redwood do KV cache and prefix caching with quantized variants?
What are the expected cost savings per 1M tokens for INT8 vs FP8 on their target instance types?
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-18 15:30 UTC | Duration: 46m | Recording: yes
Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for coming in, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, joining with Priya our SE and Marco who's owning Optimize product. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Sara Holt: Sara here, head of ML at EiraTek. We own the recommendation chat and summarization flows. Looking to cut inference cost without hurting our NPS.
[00:15] Ravi Kapoor: Ravi, platform eng. We'll run the sandbox workloads in our GCP project. Few networking constraints to flag later.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Hi, quick agenda: show Optimize console profile builder, compare INT8/FP8 snapshots, run-through tradeoffs and canary plan.
[00:27] Marco Silva: Also want to capture the fail-open/fail-closed behavior and rollback policies, since you mentioned regulatory screens.
[00:33] Tom Bowers: Our product metric: maintain answer correctness > 92% on eval set and 95th p latency < 120ms for short queries (<= 50 tokens).
[00:41] Alex Chen: Great, we'll aim the profiles at those targets.

[02:05] Priya Nair: (screen share) Opening Optimize console — here's the profile gallery, you can clone a baseline fp16 profile then create INT8 and FP8 variants. The console suggests a candidate per workload; note the fidelity lane slider which biases for speed vs fidelity.
[02:26] Sara Holt: That slider — is it deterministic? Will it pick different quant params for the same model?
[02:32] Priya Nair: It's heuristics plus sampled evals. For the same model and prompts it will pick int8 calibration tables or per-layer scale adjustments. It's not magic but it automates the most common knob turning.

[04:10] Ravi Kapoor: On infra, can we pin to specific instance types? We run on GCP A2s now.
[04:15] Marco Silva: Yes, Dedicated or Private deployments allow pinning. For hosted sandbox we approximate with n1-standard backed GPUs. For the bench we'll match your A2 config in the sandbox for a like-for-like.

[06:00] Priya Nair: Showing an example run: baseline redwood-rlm-13b fp16. INT8 gave ~3.2x token cost reduction, median latency down ~28% for 32-token responses; FP8 gave ~2.1x cost reduction and median latency down ~18%, but per-case quality delta differs.
[06:28] Tom Bowers: 3.2x is appealing — what's the worst-case quality drop?
[06:33] Priya Nair: On our internal summary benchmark, INT8 introduced a 4-6% drop in ROUGE-L vs fp16 on certain extractive tasks; FP8 was closer to 1-2%. But for chat style completion, INT8 can have edge cases with hallucinations on long-context chain-of-thought prompts.
[06:50] Sara Holt: Chain-of-thought is important for us in a small subset. Could we hybrid route those prompts to FP8/fp16?
[06:56] Alex Chen: Yes — Optimize supports routing by prompt tag or route. You can annotate the critical flows to always hit a higher-fidelity profile; the rest can go to INT8. That's a common pattern.

[09:20] Ravi Kapoor: How do you handle KV cache with quantized models — does it force full-precision caches?
[09:26] Priya Nair: Good question. We keep the KV cache layout compatible; during quantized runs the runtime uses quant-aware kernels and a quantized KV cache path where possible. For safety we allow tiered cache: prefix cache stays in fp16 for safety-critical prompts and streaming token KV can be quantized. There's a toggle in the profile to keep prefix in fp16 which reduces risk but slightly increases token cost.

[12:00] Marco Silva: We recommend a rollout: 1) calibration run on dev prompt set, 2) small bench with 1k samples, 3) 5% canary for 24-48h, 4) 25% for 48h, then ramp with automation and guardrails. In canary we collect quality deltas and user-visible metrics.

[14:15] Sara Holt: For canary, we need an automatic kill on quality regression. Does the console support guardrails?
[14:20] Marco Silva: Yes. You can set automated regression thresholds (e.g., delta > 2% on accuracy or p95 latency > 140ms) that will trigger an immediate rollback to the higher-fidelity variant and notify on-call via webhook.

[16:05] Tom Bowers: What about the cost math? We need a simple expected monthly savings for our volume (estimated 150M tokens/mo).
[16:12] Alex Chen: Rough back-of-envelope: if INT8 is 3.2x cheaper tokenwise than fp16, and you're 150M tokens, ballpark savings ~ (1 - 1/3.2) =~ 69% on model token compute bills. We'll send a modeled spreadsheet with instance costs + token weighting.
[16:25] Ravi Kapoor: Also include networking egress / cache warmup costs, please.

[18:40] Anita Shah: Security note: we need KMS integration and to ensure no PII is retained in logs. Can you confirm how logs and audit trails are handled in Private deploy?
[18:47] Dana Lee: For Private, logs stay in your VPC, keys integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and audit logs are exported to your logging endpoint. We'll share the security pack.
[18:55] Anita Shah: Great, also need SOC2 and iso docs.

[20:00] Priya Nair: Back to quality — we recommend building a small prompt set of edge cases (100-200 examples) to measure sensitivity. We'll run INT8 and FP8 and produce a degradation heatmap by intent and token length.
[20:22] Sara Holt: Can you show an example heatmap?
[20:26] Priya Nair: (shows) This one surfaces that summarization of long docs (>1k tokens) has higher drop with INT8 — directionally expected. Also certain numeric reasoning prompts degrade more.

[23:15] Tom Bowers: Is rollback instantaneous? How long to spin up fp16 nodes under load?
[23:21] Marco Silva: The platform supports instant logical rollback — traffic is routed to another profile. If the fallback requires hotter hardware (fp16 on larger GPUs), autoscaler will spin nodes which can take minutes; that's why we keep a warmed fallback lane or reserve a small pool for quick failover in Dedicated.

[25:40] Ravi Kapoor: For our constraints, network and PCIe bandwidth on A2 matters — do you have profiling we can look at?
[25:46] Priya Nair: We'll provide latency and utilization traces from our prior bench on comparable A2 shapes. They include per-kernel breakdowns and op hotspots for memory-bound layers.

[28:50] Sara Holt: About accuracy metrics — you referenced ROUGE and BLEU, we use our custom grading rubric. Will Redwood accept a tenant-provided metric for auto-regression checks?
[28:57] Alex Chen: Absolutely. The console accepts custom metrics; you can upload a small eval harness and we plug it into the automation. The guardrails evaluate those results during canary.

[31:05] Priya Nair: Walkthrough of Optimize: set baseline, clone to INT8 profile, select calibration corpus, run sampling jobs. Here's where you pick to keep prefix in fp16, whether to quantize KV, and per-layer override if you want conservative quant on attention.
[31:33] Sara Holt: Per-layer overrides — can you make them part of autosuggest?
[31:38] Marco Silva: We do; autosuggest will mark layers with high sensitivity and recommend leaving them in higher precision. You can accept suggestions or manually set.

[34:00] Tom Bowers: For production, we want a 5% canary with telemetry for 72h. We need a clear SLA for rollback and remediation.
[34:07] Alex Chen: We'll propose an SLO playbook and a runbook template. Also can include on-call page to notify Redwood CSM if automated rollback triggers.

[36:25] Ravi Kapoor: Curious about mixed-precision during streaming — does Redwood adjust precision mid-request?
[36:30] Priya Nair: We can do hybrid execution: prefix in fp16 and generative tokens in quant path, but mid-request switching has overhead. It's supported and commonly used for safety-critical prefixes.

[39:05] Anita Shah: One more on compliance: if we ingest customer prompt examples into sandbox, who owns that data and do you persist it?
[39:12] Dana Lee: Data retention is configurable. For a private deployment, EiraTek controls retention. For hosted sandbox we can set a TTL and will not use examples for model training; we'll sign that into contract language. We'll follow up with doc links.

[41:00] Priya Nair: Next steps recap: we'll provision Optimize sandbox with a demo dataset and an example profile for redwood-rlm-13b, run an initial 1k prompt sweep for INT8 and FP8, and return a degradation heatmap plus cost modeling.
[41:20] Sara Holt: Sounds good. Please include concrete canary thresholds we should put in our runbook.
[41:25] Marco Silva: We'll propose recommended thresholds: delta accuracy > 2% or p95 latency > 140ms triggers rollback. You can tighten those.

[43:10] Tom Bowers: Who's doing the bench?
[43:13] Priya Nair: Priya and team, with help from EiraTek's Ravi for infra and Anita for compliance.
[43:20] Alex Chen: OK final recap and I'll send meeting notes + sandbox invite.
[43:28] Sara Holt: Thanks everyone.
[43:31] (meeting wraps)

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-heard tokens (product names and microsecond counts), action items captured above, security pack link promised (share via CRM).
